# dsh-auth-remote
简体中文
Single-user remote sign-in for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), with password, TOTP, one-use backup codes, an
d revocable sessions. The plugin runs inside DSH and protects browser pages, APIs, streams, and WebS
able sessions. The plugin runs inside DSH and protects browser pages, APIs, streams, and WebSockets.
## Requirements

- Linux with `/proc` and Node.js 24. DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` requires Node.js `>=24.9.0`.
- A supported DSH
release and a `web` profile. One account and its sessions belong to that profile.
## DSH compatibility
Version **`0.3.5`** is prepared for release with these ten exact DSH declarations. **`0.2.2-rc.1`**
is the development default and recommended host, an upstream RC prerelease. Actual availability is e
stablished by the release workflow and npm registry. Published `0.3.4` retains its nine declarations
, including `0.2.2-alpha.3`, without retroactive RC support.

Legacy versions remain supported until an explicit retirement release; see the support policy. Newer
versions may load after capability checks, but are outside these exact compatibility declarations.
DSH `0.2.2-alpha.2` is retired in plugin `0.3.4` because fresh SDK resolution breaks native settings
updates. Upgrade to `0.2.2-rc.1`; historical plugin `0.3.3` support does not repair that host depen
dency combination. See the retirement exception.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use this npm command after the release workflow has published the version. For an offline installati
on, substitute the absolute path to the verified release archive. Published `dsh-auth-remote@0.3.3`
retains its nine declared hosts. Use the same data directory and profile for installation, initializ
ation, and the running service. These commands use DSH's default `~/.dsh` directory and the `web` pr
ofile. First rehearse upgrades in an independent profile, following the backup and rollback procedur
ile. First rehearse upgrades in an independent profile, following the backup and rollback procedure.
## Initialize the account
Run this in a real terminal:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Enter one username and a password of 12–256 Unicode characters. The password is not echoed or passed
as a command-line argument. Account creation is available only through the CLI.
TOTP is optional by default (`requireTotp: false`); the first password sign-in offers setup or skipp
ing it. Set `requireTotp: true` to require setup. Save the ten backup codes when shown: each works o
nce, and the list cannot be retrieved later.
## Configure the web profile
The minimal local setup needs no profile patch:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Open the printed `http://127.0.0.1:13090/` address. Unauthenticated navigation redirects to sign-in.
Without an explicit `publicUrl`, the plugin derives the root URL from the actual listener address,
protocol, and bound port. `/auth-remote/ready` reports service readiness.
For public access, follow the deployment guide and profile example. Set top-level `publicUrl: https:
//dsh.example.com/`, `host`, and `port`. Keep the native `webserver` independently disabled in the p
rofile patch, as shown in the example.
The listener supports concrete IPv4/IPv6 addresses, HTTP, and HTTPS with paired `tlsCert`/`tlsKey` s
ettings. `publicUrl` must be an HTTP(S) root without credentials, child paths, query, or fragment. I
t admits one public origin plus literal loopback addresses; setting it does not configure routing or
TLS. CLI listener and public-URL options override profile values. If a downstream route needs the o
riginal public Host, configure `preserveOriginPaths` as described in the deployment guide.
## Sign in and manage the account
Open the local root or your configured public URL. Inside DSH, open the sidebar account menu, then *
*Settings → Security & sign-in**. The page shows the plugin username, TOTP status, session expiry, a
nd active session count. It can change the password, set up or rebind TOTP, disable TOTP when policy
permits, and revoke sessions.
Password and second-factor changes revoke existing sessions. Sessions have a fixed default lifetime
of 168 hours (`sessionHours`) and survive service restarts. Signing out the current session preserve
s other sessions; signing out all sessions verifies the password and any bound second factor. TOTP s
etup displays backup codes once, so save and acknowledge them before signing in again.
Management commands are also available:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Mutating commands require interactive confirmation. If a submitted command loses its response, check
`status` before retrying.
Browser text supports English, Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, French, German, Russian, and Brazilian Po
rtuguese. The embedded page follows DSH's language setting. The standalone login page uses the remem
bered DSH preference, then the browser language, then English; it has no language selector. CLI outp
erence, then the browser language, then English; it has no language selector. CLI output is English.
On DSH `0.2.2-alpha.3` and `0.2.2-rc.1`, the native navigation uses a shield for this page; the othe
r eight declared hosts retain their default icon.
## Sign in to an official DeepSeek account
Remote DeepSeek account sign-in is enabled by default (`manualAccountLogin: true`):

1. Choose **Sign in** in the account menu, then **Open sign-in page** in the instruction dialog.
2.
Complete official sign-in in the new tab. The resulting loopback address may show a connection error

or 404; its page does not need to load.
3. Copy the entire callback URL, including `code` and `stat
e`, into **Full callback address** in the original DSH tab, then choose **Confirm sign-in**.
